definitions.explanation: The exact moment of 12 o'clock at night, marking the start of a new day.

examples.japanese: {午前零時|ごぜんれいじ}を{過|す}ぎた。
セールは{午前零時|ごぜんれいじ}に{始|はじ}まる。
{午前零時|ごぜんれいじ}ちょうどに{年|とし}が{変|か}わり、{花火|はなび}が{一斉|いっせい}に{打|う}ち{上|あ}がった。
examples.english: The year changed right at midnight, and fireworks were launched all at once.

notes:
A compound of {午前|ごぜん} (morning, AM) and {零時|れいじ} (zero o'clock). This is the precise, formal way to express midnight in Japanese. It is commonly used in schedules, announcements, and official contexts.

In casual speech, {夜中|よなか}の{十二時|じゅうにじ} (twelve o'clock at night) or simply {真夜中|まよなか} (the middle of the night) are more natural.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {午前零時|ごぜんれいじ}を{回|まわ}る: to pass midnight
- {午前零時|ごぜんれいじ}ちょうど: exactly at midnight
- {午前零時|ごぜんれいじ}{発|はつ}: departing at midnight

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {真夜中|まよなか}: the dead of night — refers to the general time period around midnight, not a specific clock time
- {深夜|しんや}: late at night — broader term for the late-night hours
- {日付|ひづけ}が{変|か}わる: the date changes — another way to refer to the midnight moment
